articles.title: Le Google Pixel 11 en 512 Go perd 200 € chez Amazon, avant même le début du Black Friday — Frandroid
articles.text:
Moins cher que les Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL et Pixel 11 Pro Fold, le Pixel 11 est la porte d’entrée de la gamme Pixel 11. Avec son écran de 6,3 pouces, il a le même format que le Pixel 11 Pro. Il garde quand même l’essentiel. Le téléobjectif 5x apparu sur le Pixel 10 est toujours là, avec la nouvelle puce Tensor G6 et Android 17. Lancé le 20 août à 999 euros en 256 Go et 1 129 euros en 512 Go, il démarre 100 euros plus haut que le Pixel 10 (899 euros), qui proposait encore une version 128 Go. Cette offre fait partie des premières promotions repérées avant le Black Friday, avec une baisse de 200 euros sur la version 512 Go.
Les atouts du Google Pixel 11
- Un téléobjectif 5x qui reste efficace jusqu’au zoom 30x
- Sept années de mises à jour promises par Google
- Une dalle OLED très lumineuse dans un format compact
Avec 200 euros de moins sur un prix de référence de 1 129 euros, le Pixel 11 en 512 Go tombe à 929 euros chez Amazon.
Si, par la suite, l’offre mentionnée dans cet article n’est plus disponible, merci de jeter un coup d’œil ci-dessous afin de dénicher d’autres offres concernant le Google Pixel 11 (512 Go). Le tableau s’actualise automatiquement.
Un zoom qui tient vraiment la route
La photo est le gros point fort de ce Pixel 11. Le téléobjectif 5x donne des résultats propres, y compris quand on pousse le zoom numérique jusqu’à 30x (20x au maximum sur le Pixel 10). Google a aussi agrandi son capteur grand-angle de 48 mégapixels (1/1,56 pouce, contre 1/2 pouce sur le Pixel 10), et notre test le confirme : les photos grand-angle sont de bonne qualité, les selfies aussi.
Le reste se joue sur le logiciel, avec beaucoup d’IA. La Capture magique et le mode vidéo Créateur sont les fonctions les plus réussies. La transcription et la traduction automatiques des messages vocaux servent franchement au quotidien. La fonction HiLight, ces LED colorées censées vous éviter de regarder l’écran, manque à l’appel : Google la réserve aux Pixel 11 Pro, Pro XL et Pro Fold. On l’aurait pourtant bien vue sur ce modèle.
Les concessions face aux Pixel 11 Pro
L’écran monte jusqu’à 3 000 nits en pic (2 000 nits en HDR), c’est un bon point. La dalle OLED n’est toutefois pas LTPO, une technologie que Google garde pour ses modèles Pro. La charge est l’autre limite. Google annonce une charge sans fil plus rapide (jusqu’à 25 watts avec Pixelsnap, contre 15 watts sur le Pixel 10), mais en filaire comme en sans fil, le Pixel 11 reste lent pour son prix. Google promet environ 55 % en 30 minutes avec un chargeur de 30 watts, vendu à part. Il ne gère pas non plus le Wi-Fi 7.
Pour connaître chaque critère en détail, de la photo à la recharge, lisez notre test du Google Pixel 11, réalisé par Xavier Regord.
Si un format pliable vous intéresse davantage, le Pixel 11 Pro Fold et ses concurrents sont comparés dans notre guide des meilleurs smartphones pliables.

articles.title: Le premier film généré à 100% par IA fait un flop
articles.text:
Sur les téléphones chinois, les images de synthèse font déjà recette : au mois de septembre, les mini-séries générées par IA ont dépassé les 200 milliards de vues sur Douyin, la version locale de TikTok. C’est de ce vivier qu’est sorti Sanxingdui : Future Past, adaptation d’une série courte qui cumule plus de 200 millions de vues depuis juillet 2024. Son univers puise dans les ruines de Sanxingdui, le site archéologique du Sichuan célèbre pour ses masques de bronze. Arrivé sur grand écran le 23 octobre, le premier long métrage chinois entièrement généré par IA n’a pas retrouvé son public.
Lire aussi : « Une trahison » : Martin Scorsese sous le feu des critiques pour avoir fait la promotion de l’IA dans le cinéma
Dix millions de yuans de budget, un million de recettes
Le studio Bona Film Group, coproducteur de La Bataille du lac Changjin, longtemps plus gros succès du box-office chinois, avait vu grand pour le lancement. Plus de 10 000 séances étaient programmées dès le premier jour, un volume digne d’une superproduction. Les préventes plafonnaient pourtant à 80 000 yuans, autour de 9 700 euros. Après quatre jours d’exploitation, le compteur atteignait péniblement 1,21 million de yuans, près de 145 000 euros.
La facture dépasse les 10 millions de yuans, soit environ 1,2 million d’euros. Près d’une centaine de personnes ont travaillé plus de deux ans sur le projet, générant 1,2 million d’images et plus d’une centaine de versions complètes du film. Le patron du studio, Jiang Defu, reconnaît lui-même un accueil tiède. À l’affiche au même moment, Niu Lai, un film d’animation au style volontairement rudimentaire, cumule de son côté 64,29 millions de yuans de recettes, cinquante fois plus. Les salles chinoises, elles, ne désemplissent donc pas.
Pourquoi le carton du téléphone ne paie pas la salle
L’écart entre les deux écrans tient d’abord au modèle économique. Sur Douyin, les mini-séries générées se consomment gratuitement, par épisodes de quelques minutes, entre deux vidéos. En salle, le même univers réclame un billet, un déplacement et une attention continue, face à un format qui grossit chaque défaut de génération. Le métrage long expose des visages et des mouvements que la génération d’images peine encore à tenir sur la durée, quand le format court masque les coutures.
Le secteur entier surveillait l’exercice comme un test grandeur nature. La perte sèche approche les 9 millions de yuans si la tendance se confirme. Aux États-Unis, un spécialiste du cinéma chinois prédit déjà qu’elle poussera les candidats au long métrage entièrement généré à y regarder à deux fois. Le film jouera une seconde manche à l’international, avec une sortie prévue en Malaisie le 12 novembre.

articles.title: Northflank security breach leads to abuse of customers' AI API keys
articles.text:
Cloud application hosting platform Northflank is warning customers to rotate all credentials and secrets stored on its platform after a security breach led to unauthorized use of customers' AI API keys.
Northflank is a cloud platform that allows developers to deploy and manage applications, containers, databases, and AI applications without managing the underlying infrastructure.
The company disclosed a security incident on October 30, warning customers to immediately rotate their environment variables and API keys after receiving a threat alert from cloud security company Wiz.
Soon after, Northflank told all customers to assume their environment variables had been decrypted and that the secrets stored within them were stolen.
"Assume all environment variables have been decrypted. Disable/rotate all keys," Northflank warned in an October 30 update.
Applications commonly use environment variables to store sensitive information, including database passwords, cloud service credentials, authentication tokens, and API keys.
If exposed, these credentials can be used to breach other customer services, potentially leading to data theft or unauthorized charges through API keys.
Northflank later confirmed that multiple customers had reported unauthorized use of AI API keys stored on the platform.
"Users have reported unauthorised use of AI API keys supplied to the Northflank platform," the company said.
"If you have not already rotated your user-provided secrets stored in Northflank, please do so immediately."
Customers were also advised to review their AI provider usage and billing logs for unexpected activity and report suspicious usage to Northflank and their AI providers.
According to Northflank's published incident timeline, Wiz warned them about the breach at 11:43 UTC on October 30, which the company's engineers reviewed one minute later.
Northflank quickly responded with a network policy patch, followed by additional patches at 12:50 UTC and 13:05 UTC. The company also requested assistance from Wiz's incident response team.
The company has not disclosed how attackers gained access to its systems, how many customers were affected, or whether attackers stole or abused credentials other than the reported AI API keys.
As part of its response, Northflank enabled credential rotation for PostgreSQL, MongoDB, MySQL, and Redis.
The company also enabled audit logs for all customers, including those using free accounts, to help them investigate any suspicious activity.
Northflank continues to advise customers to rotate secrets stored in workloads, secret groups, and global secrets, and to disable public access to add-ons where enabled.
BleepingComputer contacted Northflank with questions about the breach, its impact on customers, and whether stored credentials were accessed or stolen, but has not received a response.
Black October
The breach comes amid a series of attacks targeting AI development platforms, which security researchers believe are valuable targets because they store API keys that can be used to access expensive AI services.
In a report titled "Black October for AI Developer Platforms," Wiz identified at least nine security incidents affecting AI development platforms during the month, including Northflank, Railway, OpenCode, Warp, and Lightning AI.
The Railway incident also involved potential exposure of decrypted customer environment variables, while OpenCode disclosed exposed AI API keys. Warp reported a breach that exposed AI agent logs and user telemetry data.
Wiz says attackers involved in some of these incidents have specifically targeted environment variables containing AI service credentials, which can be exploited through a practice known as LLMJacking.
LLMJacking involves using stolen credentials to access AI models using another organization's API keys, generating massive API charges or allowing the stolen access to be resold.
In two cases investigated by Wiz, compromised enterprise credentials were used to make approximately 2.5 million Amazon Bedrock API calls, generating approximately $100,000 in AI usage.
The researchers also discovered infrastructure linked to services reselling access to AI models, although they could not link those operations to the initial breaches or large-scale abuse.
Wiz has not confirmed that all nine incidents were conducted by the same attackers. However, many of the incidents involved attempts to steal AI API keys.
Northflank also referenced Wiz's research in its incident updates, noting that customer reports of unauthorized AI key usage may be tied to the attacks seen by the researchers.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

articles.title: Dein Ausweis zieht aufs Handy – das musst du über d-you wissen
articles.text:
Digitale Brieftasche „d-you“: Dein Ausweis zieht aufs Smartphone – doch für 82 Prozent der Deutschen gibt es einen Haken
Die Bundesregierung plant die “digitale Brieftasche” für alle. Für die “d-you” genannte Wallet hat sie Mitte Oktober die gesetzlichen Grundlagen geschaffen, der Bundesrat muss noch zustimmen.
Starten soll die App bereits zum 2.Januar 2027. Damit setzt Deutschland Vorgaben aus der EU um. D-you ist also die deutsche Version der European Digital Identity Wallet (EUDI‑Wallet). Entwickelt wird sie von SPRIND und Common Codes im Auftrag des Bundesministeriums für Digitales und Staatsmodernisierung (BMDS).
Die Nutzung ist freiwillig. Wer kein Smartphone hat oder das digitale Angebot einfach nicht nutzen will, kann also weiter auf die physischen Ausweisdokumente zurückgreifen. Nutzen lässt sich d-you ab 16 Jahren und nur auf einem Smartphone mit NFC und Android oder iOS, alternative Betriebssysteme werden nicht unterstützt. Außerdem braucht die Ausweisfunktion eine Internetverbindung. Geht das Handy verloren, muss die Wallet ohne Backup komplett neu eingerichtet werden.
Behörden, die für ihre Online-Dienste einen elektronischen Ausweis verlangen, müssen d-you als Identifizierungsdienst akzeptieren. Ab Ende 2027 sind dann auch Banken, Energieversorger, Telekommunikationsanbieter und sehr große Online-Plattformen verpflichtet, die Wallet zu nutzen. Normale Online-Shops entscheiden dagegen selbst, ob sie d-you integrieren.
Was kann die digitale Brieftasche d-you?
Die Wallet bringt im Prinzip die Möglichkeit, sich online und digital auszuweisen, etwa bei Behördengängen, im Online-Shopping oder bei Vertragsabschlüssen. Das gilt nicht nur in Deutschland: Weil alle EU-Staaten so eine Wallet bereitstellen müssen und die Wallets in allen Mitgliedstaaten gelten, wird man d-you auch im EU-Ausland nutzen können.
Insbesondere das Identifizierungsverfahren soll dann einfacher ablaufen, als etwa beim bisher häufig genutzten Videoident-Verfahren. Während man dabei einem Service-Mitarbeiter den Ausweis vorzeigen muss, werden in der Wallet wenige Klicks genügen, um die eigene Identität zu bestätigen.
D-you baut dabei auf dem Personalausweis mit Online-Funktion auf. Nach einer einmaligen Anmeldung wird eine digitale Kopie der Identitätsdaten auf dem Handy gespeichert, danach muss der Ausweis nicht mehr wie bislang bei jedem einzelnen Vorgang ans Telefon gehalten werden.
Perspektivisch sollst du in d-you alle möglichen behördlichen Dokumente, aber auch andere Unterlagen und Tickets speichern und die App für Behördengänge, die Eröffnung von Bankkonten oder den Abschluss von Verträgen nutzen können. Außerdem soll sie etwa beim Einkaufen einen einfachen Altersnachweis ermöglichen.
Allerdings könnte der Starttermin noch wackeln, das Digitalministerium will „unter Berücksichtigung eventueller Restrisiken” über den Start entscheiden. Sicher ist: Die App wird zum geplanten Start im Januar noch nicht alle Funktionen haben.
„Zum Launch wird es keinen großen ‚Big Bang‘ geben“, sagt Johannes Hollunder, der sich beim Digitalverband Bitkom mit digitalen Identifizierungsverfahren beschäftigt. Es gehe darum, Schritt für Schritt Anwendungen in die Wallet zu integrieren, die wirklich funktionieren. “Das volle Potenzial von d-you wird sich entfalten, wenn mehr Partner ihre Anwendungsfälle in die Wallet integrieren.“
Ein großer Vorteil der Wallet soll darin liegen, dass sich nicht nur staatliche, sondern auch private Dokumente in die Wallet laden lassen, neben Ausweis und Führerschein etwa das Deutschlandticket, die Zugangskarte fürs Fitnessstudio oder ein Konzertticket. Doch diese Funktionen werden erst nach und nach integriert werden. Mit einer großen Einführungskampagne wird das Digitalministerium also wahrscheinlich warten, bis die Wallet auch wirklich viel zu bieten hat.
Anfangs wird auf jeden Fall der digitale Ausweis und dann etwas später auch der Führerschein, Sozialpass oder Rentenausweis verfügbar sein. Außerdem arbeiten rund 40 Partner wie etwa die Deutsche Post, die Sparkassen, Vodafone und Rossmann an Funktionen für d-you. Ob alle Partner direkt zum Start Funktionen bereitstellen werden, ist noch nicht klar. Die Sparkassen kündigen zum Start immerhin zehn Anwendungen an, etwa zur Identifizierung bei der Eröffnung von Konten und Depots. Später sollen auch Freigaben im Online-Banking und von Zahlungen hinzukommen.
Auch in der Verwaltung wird d-you erst schrittweise ankommen. Bundesbehörden müssen ihre Nachweise bis Ende 2027 elektronisch in der Wallet ausstellen können. „Wer ein Dokument von einer Bundesbehörde braucht, kann es also spätestens zwölf Monate nach dem Start elektronisch erhalten“, erklärt Hollunder. Das gilt jedoch nur auf Bundesebene. In den Ländern und Kommunen hängt die Frage, ob und wann diese eigene Nachweise in die Wallet ausstellen, dagegen auch vom Stand der Technik und dem Budget ab.
„Anfangs könnte es also sein, dass eine Kommune Dokumente bereitstellt, während eine andere das noch nicht tut“, sagt Hollunder. Aktuell wird eine zentrale Plattform entwickelt, um diese Dokumente auszustellen. Wie schnell die Kommunen sich daran anbinden, hängt dann von ihren Kapazitäten ab.
Das brauchst du, um d-you zu nutzen
Die Anmeldung bei d-you wird über den Ausweis mit Online-Funktion laufen. Nutzer geben dazu bei der ersten Anmeldung die sechsstellige PIN des Online-Ausweises ein, die App liest die Karte per NFC aus und vergibt dann eine eigene sechsstellige PIN für die Wallet. Für die Übernahme der Identitätsdaten werden dazu Softwarekomponenten der Ausweis-App genutzt.
Das bedeutet allerdings auch: Falls du keinen funktionierenden Online-Ausweis hast oder deine PIN für die Online-Funktion vergessen hast, bekommst du auch keinen Zugang zu d-you.
Für die d-you-Nutzung könnte das zu einer echten Hürde werden. Denn obwohl der Online-Ausweis seit 2010 in jedem neuen Personalausweis angelegt ist, wird er nur von einem Bruchteil der Bevölkerung genutzt. Laut einer Bitkom-Umfrage im April haben nur 18 Prozent der Befragten die Online-Funktion aktiviert und kennen ihre PIN. Weitere 21 Prozent haben die Funktion zwar freigeschaltet, kennen ihre PIN aber nicht mehr.
Wer die PIN vergessen oder die Online-Funktion im Ausweis bislang nicht genutzt hat, kann kostenlos einen Rücksetzbrief anfordern und erhält dann per Post entsprechende Zugangsdaten.
Datenschutz und Sicherheit bei d-you
Die digitale Brieftasche speichert Nachweise nicht nur als bloße Abbilder. Die Dokumente sind kryptografisch signiert und kommen direkt von der ausstellenden Behörde. Anbieter von anderen Funktionen können ihre Echtheit also jederzeit überprüfen. Die Wallet verspricht ein datensparsames Design, soll also möglichst wenig Daten der Nutzer weitergeben.
Beim Altersnachweis etwa im Supermarkt soll die Wallet künftig etwa nur bestätigen, dass jemand volljährig ist, ohne Name und Adresse preiszugeben. Ob das aber zum Start schon funktioniert und auch an der Kasse ohne Internetverbindung, ist offen.
Grundsätzlich müssen Partner der Wallet offenlegen, wofür sie welche Daten brauchen. Und bekommen nur Zugriff auf diese Informationen. Eine Vorabprüfung, ob Unternehmen nur die Daten abfragen, die sie wirklich brauchen, sieht das Gesetz aber nicht vor. Wer kein biometrisches Passfoto in der Wallet haben will, kann das ablehnen. Außerdem entscheidet der Nutzer vor jeder Übermittlung selbst, ob er Daten teilen will.
Kritiker sehen darin allerdings auch ein Problem. So warnte die Sachverständige Bianca Kastl vom Innovationsverbund Öffentliche Gesundheit in einer Anhörung der Bundestags vor einem „Cookie-Banner 2.0“-Szenario. Wer eine Anfrage vorschnell bestätigt, gibt dann vielleicht mehr preis als nötig. Verbraucherschützer kritisieren zudem, dass die App zum Start noch keine pseudonyme Nutzung ermöglicht, sie soll erst später kommen.
Fragezeichen gibt es auch noch bei der Sicherheitsarchitektur. Die Daten sollen langfristig im Secure Element des Handys gespeichert werden. Zunächst sollen die Schlüssel aber nicht im Handy, sondern in Hochsicherheitsmodulen auf Servern gespeichert werden. Das Projekt begründet das damit, dass die EU für den digitalen Ausweis das höchste Sicherheitsniveau verlangt und nur wenige Smartphones den dafür nötigen Spezialchip besitzen.
Das Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik (BSI) und der Bundesdatenschutzbeauftragte warnten außerdem davor, dass die staatlich signierten Daten auch nach einem Leck als echt nachweisbar bleiben und damit ein lohnendes Ziel für Datenhändler und Betrüger sind.
Das Digitalministerium hat im Oktober ein Bug-Bounty-Programm gestartet und belohnt das Aufspüren von Sicherheitslücken.
Auch die Deutsche Kreditwirtschaft als Interessenvertretung der Banken forderte zuletzt noch Nachbesserungen, etwa zu Haftungsregeln. Bei Fehlern soll aus ihrer Sicht der Wallet-Anbieter haften und nicht die Bank. Eine Pflicht, Zahlungen über d-you anzubieten, lehnt sie ab.

articles.title: Parece que han encontrado a la culpable de la rotura de la pantalla de algunos iPhone Duo. Y esto pone la campaña navideña a tiritar
articles.text:
El iPhone Duo se puso a la venta hace justo una semana y no hemos tenido que esperar demasiado para ver los primeros errores. Al margen de apps de terceros sin optimizar, algo lógico y que se irá solucionando, durante el primer fin de semana aparecieron usuarios que compartieron fotos de pantallas rotas en sus dispositivos. Todas tenían el mismo patrón de rotura y pronto se apuntó al mecanismo que podría tener la culpa.
Ahora parece que ya han encontrado esa pieza.
Qué ha pasado. Primero fue en Reddit, pero luego se fue extendiendo. Varios usuarios han reportado que, durante los primeros usos, el flamante iPhone Duo se rompía. Que haya unidades que salgan con fallos de fábrica, da igual que sea una nueva generación o no, es algo habitual porque se fabrican millones y es normal que algunas pasen bajo el radar de las pruebas de calidad, pero aquí el patrón era raro.
Una línea horizontal de píxeles muertos que cruza la parte derecha de la pantalla interior y una línea vertical justo en la bisagra que podía ser más o menos visible, pero que también estaba presente. Lo curioso del asunto es que esa línea horizontal era igual en todos los modelos con la pantalla rota, lo que llevó a pensar que detrás quizá había algo más que un problema de control de calidad en un lote..
La culpable. iFixit pronto hizo un vídeo en el que mostraban, usando radiografías y simulación, la posible pieza culpable. Comentaron que había un refuerzo estructural para mantener la zona central estable cuando extendemos la pantalla, pero que al doblarla, genera una enorme tensión sobre el panel y las conexiones, lo que podía terminar provocando el error.
Ahora, un youtuber surcoreano se ha dejado de radiografías y ha compartido este vídeo en el que podemos ver exactamente la pieza en cuestión:
iFixit ha hecho otro vídeo en el que se apoyan en lo que cuenta ese youtuber y aportan imágenes que muestran cómo, con la pantalla apagada, se puede ver en alguna unidad esa pieza que está causando el error. El medio especialista en reparación de dispositivos ratifica el vídeo del youtuber surcoreano, aportando nuevas simulaciones y escáneres que nos permiten ver el funcionamiento de esa pieza y cómo causa el error.
Prisas. El propio medio comenta que es temprano para hablar de cuántas unidades están afectadas, ya que tampoco es que haya demasiadas en el mercado, y no se aventura a decir que sea un fallo de diseño generalizado como fue el de la Xbox 360 original, el del teclado de mariposa del MacBook 2017 o el del Galaxy Note 7, pero sí que está afectando a cierto número de modelos.
A través de GSM Arena, podemos leer un informe del medio chino Jiemian News en el que un trabajador anónimo de Foxconn comenta que Apple habría reducido sus estándares de inspección de calidad con el objetivo de tener todas las unidades posible a tiempo tanto para el lanzamiento como para una campaña navideña que peligra. Ese empleado también comenta que la línea de producción del iPhone Duo
No es la primera vez que eso de las prisas por sacar el iPhone plegable sale a relucir. A comienzos de septiembre, antes de que se presentara el plegable, desde Nikkei Asia apuntaron que Apple no estaba pudiendo fabricar todos los plegables que quería. De hecho, se decía que no era un problema de diseño o de componentes, sino consecuencia del exigente nivel de calidad autoimpuesto.
Consecuencias. Si se han visto con el agua al cuello es algo que no podemos saber, pero lo cierto es que, si hoy entras en la web de Apple a por un plegable, la fecha que te dan para recogerlo es a meses vista. El 25 de enero, para ser exactos, por lo que se pierden la jugosísima campaña navideña.
Más allá del stock, está la consecuencia más directa, y es la posible crisis reputacional si el número de móviles afectados continúa aumentando. La bisagra es el componente más complejo de un plegable y un fallo de diseño en la misma no es algo que se solucione de la noche a la mañana.
Qué dice Apple. La compañía mantiene el comunicado temprano que hizo a comienzos de semana:
"Somos conscientes de un problema que afecta a la pantalla interior en un pequeño número de unidades del iPhone Duo. Si los usuarios experimentan problemas con la pantalla de su iPhone Duo, deben ponerse en contacto con AppleCare para obtener un reemplazo"
Por nuestra parte, hemos preguntado directamente a Apple debido a la actualización de la información sobre la pieza protagonista de esta historia y actualizaremos tan pronto como tengamos novedades. En nuestro análisis del iPhone Duo no tuvimos ningún problema, pero si estuviera interesado en comprar uno, esperaría a ver qué pasa.

articles.title: Grok de Elon Musk lanza el primer episodio de “Odyssey” generado por inteligencia artificial
articles.text:
Grok Imagine ha publicado el primer capítulo de su adaptación de “La Odisea”. Se trata de un vídeo de unos 7 minutos que ha llegado a X. Está hecho con la herramienta de creación audiovisual de Elon Musk. Además del propio Grok Imagine, han trabajado en él de forma creativa Wonder Studios y el director Dev Walker (que trabaja en cine con IA).
“Mira el episodio 1 de nuestra serie Odyssey, hecha con Grok Imagine”, dice la publicación. La cuenta invita a pedir un detalle de cómo se ha hecho este episodio.
La promesa de Musk y sus críticas a Nolan
Además, Musk había anunciado en julio que antes de que acabase el año Grok Imagine iba a hacer un largometraje de La Odisea “históricamente preciso y fiel al arte de Homero”. Acompañó el anuncio con un corto (de 3 minutos) que había hecho otro usuario con IA. El estreno en octubre es el inicio de una serie. El plazo que daba Musk para la película es hasta diciembre.
Esta iniciativa viene después de sus críticas a la adaptación de Christopher Nolan (sobre todo por la decisión de elegir a Elliot Page y Lupita Nyong’o). Lo vinculó a la búsqueda de premios. También acusó al director de ser “racista antiblancos”.
Por otra parte, también reaccionó el director Scott Derrickson (“Doctor Strange”, “The Black Phone”), que rechazó sus opiniones sobre cine. “Sus opiniones sobre arte no valen nada”.
Una de estas acusaciones tiene más detalle porque está relacionada con los requisitos de los Óscar. La Academia establece que, para poder optar a mejor película, deben cumplirse dos de los cuatro estándares de representación e inclusión. Algunos de ellos tienen que ver con los equipos y oportunidades de formación. Es posible cumplir estos requisitos sin tener que pasar por el de representación en pantalla. No hay obligatoriedad de contar con estos actores.
Qué permite hacer Grok Imagine
Para entender cómo funciona la herramienta, tenemos que entrar en detalle de sus características. En el anuncio de Video 1.5 (16 de junio de 2026) se describe cómo es capaz de generar los efectos sonoros y ambiente (y diálogos) junto a las imágenes. Esto no permite inferir cómo se ha hecho la banda sonora.
En esta misma presentación aparecía un tráiler de “Odyssey” que hacía David Thompson (Heavy Pulp). Por otro lado, la compañía también anunciaba otras funcionalidades relacionadas con el manejo de material. Por ejemplo, búsquedas en la biblioteca de imágenes y vídeos.
El 31 de julio se añadieron referencias visuales y de voz. Con ellas era posible mantener un personaje en distintos escenarios. Se podían utilizar hasta 7 imágenes de referencia por generación. De esta forma se facilita el montaje de una secuencia. Se pueden utilizar los materiales previos para dirigir las nuevas tomas. No es necesario describir cada plano únicamente con texto.
También se añadió la posibilidad de empezar con un vídeo desde una descripción (sin imagen inicial) y la generación nativa a 1080p. Estas son algunas de las características generales de Video 1.5. En el anuncio del episodio no se indica cuál es la versión que se ha usado. Tampoco se confirma que hayan utilizado todas las funciones.
En la documentación de generación de vídeo (actualizada el 10 de octubre) se indica que la duración de una generación es configurable (entre 1 y 15 segundos). Con ese funcionamiento documentado, para generar 7 minutos hacen falta varios clips. La duración final no corresponde a una única petición.
Nosotros ya hablamos de la capacidad de Grok para generar imágenes realistas. En este episodio podemos analizar una producción más extensa (se indican los créditos creativos). Nos queda por saber el coste y el proceso de selección/montaje. El anuncio invita a pedir un detalle de cómo han hecho este episodio.

articles.title: Stablecoins gain ground in Africa but face hurdles to use
articles.text:
Stablecoins are giving African businesses an alternative way to pay overseas suppliers, but costs, security concerns and fragmented blockchain networks remain obstacles to wider use, industry executives told Moonshot by TechCabal in Lagos.
Speaking on a panel titled, “Where Are Stablecoins Creating Real Value in Africa?”, representatives from Solana Superteam Nigeria, Obiex and Hyperbridge said demand was being driven by practical difficulties in accessing foreign currency and completing international payments.
Chinonso Obiefule, lead at Solana Superteam Nigeria, said some Nigerian businesses were already using stablecoins to pay suppliers in China when dollars were difficult to obtain through conventional channels.
“People want to access dollars, but they cannot do that because, obviously, dollars aren’t easily accessible, so the next best option is actually stablecoin,” he said.
The appeal extends beyond access to foreign currency. Businesses trading across time zones also need to move funds outside banking hours, said Odinaka Esiagu, head of customer success and operations at Obiex.
A company buying goods from a Chinese supplier might need to complete a payment while its bank was closed, she said. Stablecoins could allow it to transfer funds without waiting until the next banking day.
Esiagu said the technology would improve the flexibility of certain transactions rather than eliminate the need for banks.
The discussion reflected the growing role of dollar-linked digital assets in Nigeria’s financial system. The country received about $59 billion in crypto-asset inflows between July 2023 and June 2024, according to the IMF.
That figure covers crypto assets broadly, rather than stablecoins alone. The fund also estimates that Nigeria has accounted for roughly 60 per cent of stablecoin inflows into sub-Saharan Africa since 2019.
Costs and confidence
For businesses, however, a new payment channel must offer more than availability. Obiefule said developers needed to make international transfers cheaper, safer and easier to use.
“It should be cheaper to send money to somebody abroad or to get money from somebody abroad,” he said.
Low blockchain transaction fees were an important consideration for companies choosing which networks to use, he added. Lower costs could make stablecoin payments commercially viable for more businesses.
Trust remained another constraint. Esiagu said reports of cryptocurrency platforms being hacked continued to deter potential customers.
“Some people are still scared,” she said.
Obiex was developing a service to help businesses build stablecoin-based products by providing technical and compliance-related support, she added. The aim was to allow companies to focus on their customers without having to develop all the underlying capabilities themselves.
Connecting separate networks
Seun Lanlege, chief executive of Hyperbridge, said fragmentation across blockchains created a further challenge: funds available on one network were not necessarily readily accessible on another.
That limited users’ ability to draw on liquidity across platforms, complicating the promise of seamless transfers.
Lanlege said Hyperbridge provided infrastructure for moving tokens between networks, while its HyperFX product used those connections to facilitate transactions across blockchain ecosystems.
Such systems needed to prioritise security and decentralisation, he argued, warning that reliance on centralised intermediaries could create vulnerabilities.
Regulation also remains central to the market’s development. The IMF has called for clearer treatment of stablecoin issuers in Nigeria, alongside stronger oversight and better data on how digital assets interact with the domestic financial system.
It has warned that widespread use of dollar-denominated stablecoins could weaken monetary policy transmission and create financial integrity risks.

articles.title: Intel stock plunges nearly 30%, its worst day in 52 years
articles.text:
What just happened? Intel was one of the stock market's biggest surprises this year. Its shares nearly quadrupled between January and a record high in late June – a run fueled by demand for the CPUs behind agentic AI. But on Friday, the chipmaker gave back a huge chunk of those gains in a single session. The stock closed down almost 29% at $65.76, its worst day since 1974.
Oddly enough, the quarter itself went well. Intel beat Wall Street's earnings estimates. Its data center revenue jumped nearly 80% from a year earlier to $7.3 billion, too. But its forecast for the last three months of the year landed well short: analysts had penciled in about $17 billion in revenue. Intel only expects $15 billion to $16 billion.
The weak spot is PCs. AI data centers are buying up so much of the world's memory that laptops and desktops have gotten a lot pricier this year. So fewer of them are selling. Intel now expects PC shipments to drop about 12% in 2026 and another 10% in 2027. It doesn't see things improving until memory supply and prices get back to normal.
The forecast also has to absorb a shutdown at the company's fab in Kiryat Gat, Israel. That's where an explosion killed two workers earlier this month.
Going by Yahoo Finance's count of closing prices back to 1973, only a nearly 30% slide in July 1974 was worse than Friday. Bank of America, D.A. Davidson, Seaport and Roth all downgraded the stock to neutral the same day. The US government felt it too, since its roughly 10% stake lost about $12 billion in paper value. Even so, Washington's shares are still worth over three times the $20.47 apiece it paid last year.
Intel's slide came a day after Alphabet's worst session ever. The Google parent shed roughly $500 billion in market value on Thursday after its quarterly report showed AI infrastructure spending had pushed free cash flow $9.07 billion into the red.
Meta's earnings didn't land much better. Both it and Alphabet now sit more than 20% below their 52-week highs, according to Yahoo Finance data. Even Nvidia is about 12% off its peak, mostly because investors fear its biggest customers will have to scale back spending in 2027.
Over in Seoul, SK Hynix fell 7% and Samsung lost 3% on Friday. That pulled South Korea's KOSPI down nearly 3.5%. Both companies make the memory that AI data centers have been soaking up, so the same boom squeezing Intel's PC business is now rattling investors in the boom's biggest winners.
For anyone shopping for a PC, none of this points to cheaper hardware soon. Memory prices could keep climbing through next year. Some forecasts don't have real relief arriving until 2028.

articles.title: Cambridge scientists create a $10 chip that could put a medical lab on your wrist
articles.text:
Cambridge scientists create a $10 chip that could put a medical lab on your wrist
- Date:
- October 22, 2026
- Source:
- University of Cambridge
- Summary:
- Cambridge researchers have created a groundbreaking $10 optical sensor that delivers the precision of laboratory equipment in a device small enough for wearable technology. It identified foods, plastics, and medicines with 100% accuracy in tests and demonstrated the ability to monitor blood glucose, alcohol, and other health markers without invasive procedures.
- Share:
A new optical sensor costing just $10 could bring laboratory-level precision to wearable health monitors, potentially allowing people to track blood glucose without needles. The technology could also transform food testing, industrial quality control, and environmental monitoring.
Researchers at the University of Cambridge and GlitterinTech (a start-up founded by the same research group) have developed a new type of optical spectrometer that combines exceptional accuracy with a remarkably small size and low cost. Measuring just centimeters across, the device could be incorporated into portable electronics and wearable health technology. Its potential applications range from monitoring important health markers in real time to identifying materials and detecting changes in chemical composition.
Optical spectrometers work by analyzing light to reveal information about the substances it interacts with. They are essential tools in medicine, manufacturing, chemical testing, and environmental research. However, making these instruments smaller has traditionally meant compromising their performance. Compact spectrometers often have limited measurement ranges, reduced resolution, or lower accuracy, making them better suited to identifying substances than performing precise measurements.
The researchers believe their new design could overcome these limitations. Known as a convolutional spectrometer, it uses a mathematical principle called the convolution theorem to analyze light in a fundamentally different way. According to the team, this approach delivers performance that surpasses existing types of spectrometers in several key areas, including designs based on light dispersion, Fourier transforms, and computational reconstruction.
A New Way to Analyze Light With Extraordinary Precision
Traditional spectrometers generally separate incoming light into its component wavelengths or use complex calculations to reconstruct its spectrum. The new device takes another approach by performing a mathematical operation called convolution directly on the incoming light.
To accomplish this, the researchers arranged optical components with repeating spectral responses in a sequence. These components can include unbalanced Mach-Zehnder interferometers or micro-ring resonators. By adjusting them in proportion to one another, the system can shift its response to different wavelengths in a controlled, linear fashion. Fast Fourier transforms are then used to accurately recover the light spectrum.
"The key insight was to go back to the mathematics and ask whether there was a fundamentally cleaner way to retrieve spectra," said Dr. Chunhui Yao, a lead author of the study. "By using the convolution theorem directly in the optical domain, we avoid many of the limitations that have held miniaturized spectrometers back. This gives us high precision, strong noise tolerance, and very low computational overhead, all in a compact and low-cost system."
The researchers built the spectrometer using a silicon nitride photonic platform and integrated it with onboard electronics. It operates across a broad range of near-infrared wavelengths (1200-1700 nm) and can collect and process measurements in less than a second.
Another important advantage is its ability to expand its measurement capabilities without major hardware changes. Because the system uses repeating optical patterns, its spectral bandwidth can theoretically be extended almost without limit. Adding more optical components in sequence can also increase its resolution exponentially.
A $10 Sensor That Could Transform Food Testing and Healthcare
To evaluate the device outside purely theoretical measurements, the researchers tested it on a variety of materials and substances. The results demonstrated its potential for applications that normally depend on larger, more expensive laboratory instruments.
When used to identify plastics, pharmaceuticals, coffee, flour, and tea, the spectrometer achieved a 100% classification success rate in the reported tests. It also measured concentrations in water-based and organic solutions with accuracies of approximately 0.01%, exceeding the performance of commercial benchtop spectrometers in those experiments.
The healthcare demonstrations were particularly promising. Under conditions designed to reflect real physiological environments, the device accurately measured several human biomarkers, including skin moisture, blood alcohol, blood lactate, and blood glucose.
The researchers also demonstrated noninvasive glucose tracking over an extended period in one participant. Although further testing would be needed before the technology could become a practical medical product, the finding suggests a possible route toward monitoring blood sugar without repeatedly piercing the skin.
"These biomedical demonstrations are particularly exciting," said Prof. Qixiang Cheng, who led the project. "What makes this work stand out is not just performance in the lab, but technical readiness. Dr. Chunhui Yao's contribution was crucial in translating a mathematical concept into a fully packaged, robust system that operates reliably across temperature extremes and real-world conditions. That combination is what opens the door to practical deployment."
The sensor also demonstrated impressive resistance to temperature changes. It continued operating reliably between -20°C and 80°C, an unusually wide temperature range for a miniature spectrometer. This durability could be especially valuable for wearable devices, factory equipment, and sensors operating outdoors.
Why a Simpler Design Could Be a Major Breakthrough
The new spectrometer's advantages extend beyond its accuracy, size, and price. Its internal design also reduces the amount of computing power needed to analyze incoming light.
Many existing miniature spectrometers depend on complicated calibration procedures and demanding algorithms to reconstruct spectral information. These methods can become unreliable when measurements contain noise, and they often require substantial processing resources.
The Cambridge team's convolution-based approach avoids much of this complexity. Because the measurements follow a linear mathematical relationship, the system can recover spectra rapidly and consistently while using relatively little computational power.
"This is a beautiful example of how elegant engineering can unlock real impact," said Prof. Richard Penty, who contributed to the photonic system design and integration. "The architecture is simple, scalable, and manufacturable, yet it delivers precision that rivals or exceeds much larger instruments. Dr. Chunhui Yao played a central role in bringing together the photonic design, system integration, and experimental validation that made this possible."
Its relatively simple construction could also make the technology easier to manufacture on a large scale, potentially bringing sophisticated optical measurements to devices where conventional spectrometers would be too bulky or expensive.
Bringing Laboratory-Grade Measurements to Everyday Devices
The researchers envision a future in which accurate optical sensing becomes a routine feature of everyday technology rather than something largely confined to specialized laboratories.
In industrial settings, inexpensive spectrometers could be installed throughout manufacturing facilities to continuously check material composition and product quality. Similar sensors could monitor food freshness, identify substances, and analyze environmental conditions on a much larger scale than is currently practical.
Healthcare could see equally significant changes. Compact sensors might eventually enable wearables to measure hydration levels, detect signs of alcohol intoxication, track biomarkers related to physical fitness, or continuously monitor glucose levels for people managing diabetes.
"Our vision is to make spectrometry as ubiquitous as temperature or motion sensing," added Prof. Qixiang Cheng. "This work shows that high-quality spectral information doesn't have to be confined to the laboratory -- it can be embedded directly into the technologies people use every day."
As photonic technology becomes smaller and more advanced, the convolutional spectrometer provides a promising example of how mathematical insights and practical engineering can make sophisticated scientific instruments simpler, cheaper, and more accessible. By combining high precision with a device that costs around $10, the researchers have opened a potential path toward a new generation of smart sensors capable of measuring the hidden chemistry of our bodies and surroundings.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Cambridge. Original written by Michael Shuff. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Chunhui Yao, Jie Ma, Ningning Wang, Peng Bao, Wei Zhuo, Tao Zhang, Wanlu Zhang, Kangning Xu, Ting Yan, Liang Ming, Yuxiao Ye, Tawfique Hasan, Ian White, Richard Penty, Qixiang Cheng. Optical convolutional spectrometer. Nature Photonics, 2026; 20 (6): 664 DOI: 10.1038/s41566-026-01891-6

articles.title: Vic Mensa can’t live without the Voice Memos app
articles.text:
Vic Mensa is one of those people who has done so many things that it’s hard to remember where you were first introduced to him. Was it his debut mixtape Innanetape, which finally hit the major streaming services for the first time in September? Or maybe his house-influenced single “Down On My Luck”? Maybe you didn’t even realize that Mensa was a rapper. Maybe you know him from his roles on The Chi or Bel-Air. Or perhaps you’re mostly aware of him through his activism, social media presence (peeling oranges and waxing poetic), or his podcast The Vic Mensa Show.
Vic Mensa can’t live without the Voice Memos app
Between his music, acting, podcast, activism, and businesses, Vic Mensa wears a lot of hats.
Vic Mensa can’t live without the Voice Memos app
Between his music, acting, podcast, activism, and businesses, Vic Mensa wears a lot of hats.
Point is, the man wears many hats. Part of the secret to being so prolific, it turns out, is Voice Memos. Just capture those ideas before they disappear.
What is your most indispensable tool?
Voice Memos. Everything starts there for me. Songs, essay ideas, orange tree thoughts, voice notes to myself at some wild hour, little things my son says that I do not want to lose. My phone is a million distractions in one rectangle, but Voice Memos is one of the few parts of it that still feels honest. Just press record before the thought disappears.
Which social media platform do you use the most?
Instagram, for better or worse. That’s definitely where my voice has really found its legs. I started out peeling an orange and talking through whatever was on my mind, and it turned into this whole conversation with people about politics, history, music, grief, jokes, fatherhood, all of it. That response helped show me there was room for The Vic Mensa Show too. Instagram can be a circus, obviously, but it’s also a very valuable tool for connection.
Which tech trend do you wish would go away?
Maybe Meta glasses. Them motherfuckers seem like they’re being used for evil.
What creation are you most proud of?
Probably my upcoming album right now. It’s the first album that I’ve really taken myself completely seriously as a producer. The surrounding art, videos, design, clothing, and world I’m building around it is something that really excites me as well.
What do you do when you need to focus?
I either do my Shambhavi Mahamudra meditation that I learned from Sadhguru or the Wim Hof breathing method. Ideally, I’ll do the Wim Hof breathing method in the steam room and then the meditation.
What do you think is worth splurging on?
Anything that touches your life every day. A good mattress. Good headphones. Quality food. Clothes you will actually keep for years. Experiences with your child. I have wasted money on plenty of dumb shit, so I am trying to be better about buying things that either last or make a real memory.
What would the tagline for your biopic be?
Live from the contradiction.
What is the last GIF or meme you used?

articles.title: Rian Johnson (Star Wars VIII, Knives Out) sort une app de caméra à 15 € et elle est déjà top 1 sur l'App Store
articles.text:
Il y a 1 000 façons de rater une photo avec un iPhone, notamment parce qu’Apple n’est pas allé aussi loin dans l’accompagnement algorithmique des utilisateurs que Google avec ses Pixel. Depuis quelques années, le traitement d’Apple (HDR intelligent, Deep Fusion, Photonic Engine…) produit des images d’une netteté redoutable, mais aussi d’une uniformité qui commence à lasser les photographes. C’est pour cela qu’Apple a sorti récemment ses Styles, qui ne sont pas des filtres et qui permettent de reprendre la main sur des tas de paramètres. À titre perso, les Styles m’ont complètement réconcilié avec les photos à l’iPhone.
Rian Johnson, lui, fait visiblement partie des lassés, mais pour lui, les Styles ne sont pas suffisants.
« J’ai récemment harcelé mon directeur de la photo pour qu’il me fabrique mon app photo idéale pour iPhone. » C’est ainsi que le cinéaste a présenté Chromagraph Camera sur X le 28 octobre 2026, dans un message vu plus de 11 millions de fois. Le directeur de la photo en question, c’est Steve Yedlin, qui a signé l’image de tous ses films depuis Brick en 2005, de Looper à Wake Up Dead Man, le dernier Knives Out.
Il a développé l’app avec Eric Cameron, dev spécialisé en science des couleurs. Johnson raconte qu’il voulait simplement l’outil pour lui-même, parce qu’il prend énormément de photos avec son téléphone, et que ses deux complices ont décidé de la publier (super le storytelling, mais on y croit moyen).
Que fait Chromagraph pour 15 € ?
L’app capture en RAW, ignore entièrement le traitement d’image de l’iPhone et lui substitue celui que Yedlin applique sur les films de Johnson, adapté au comportement des capteurs d’Apple. L’éditeur insiste sur la nuance : un filtre se pose sur une image déjà traitée par le téléphone, alors que Chromagraph repart des données brutes du capteur. Exactement comme les Styles d’Apple.
Autre parti pris, emprunté à l’argentique : on cadre, on déclenche, et on ne découvre le rendu final qu’en ouvrant la galerie. L’app permet ensuite d’ajuster couleur, exposition, grain et halo lumineux (la « halation », ce léger débordement de lumière autour des hautes lumières propre à la pellicule), sans toucher au fichier RAW d’origine, conservé dans l’app. Les photos s’exportent en JPEG ou HEIC vers la photothèque, éventuellement de façon automatique.
Rian Johnson a lui-même listé les limites dans la foulée : pas de vidéo pour l’instant, l’équipe y réfléchit, mais ce ne serait sans doute possible que sur les derniers iPhone Pro (ce ne serait pas le premier ni le dernier à verrouiller du logiciel sur un matériel spécifique). Et pas d’Android : l’homogénéité du matériel d’Apple est ce qui permet à une si petite équipe de calibrer le rendu avec confiance, explique-t-il, quand la diversité des smartphones Android l’en empêche.
Le look Yedlin dans la poche
Pour comprendre le succès de l’app, il faut connaître Steve Yedlin. Le chef opérateur défend depuis des années, démonstrations vidéo à l’appui, une thèse qui agace une partie de la profession : le « look » d’un film doit bien plus à la façon dont on traite les images qu’à la caméra qui les a captées. Chromagraph est l’application grand public de cette idée. Votre iPhone reste un iPhone, mais il hérite de la même chaîne de traitement que les films de Johnson.
Évidemment, ce rendu est un parti pris assumé. Ceux qui aiment les photos d’iPhone telles qu’elles sortent de l’appareil risquent de trouver le rendu un peu sombre. L’idée de court-circuiter le traitement d’Apple n’est pas neuve non plus : Halide, l’app photo de référence des puristes, propose déjà un mode qui fait la même chose. La différence tient à la signature : Halide vous rend une image brute, Chromagraph vend le regard d’un chef opérateur.
Côté pratique, l’app coûte 14,99 € en France (12,99 dollars aux États-Unis), en achat unique, sans abonnement ni achat intégré (une rareté devenue presque exotique sur l’App Store), demande iOS 17 ou plus, et l’éditeur déclare ne collecter aucune donnée.

articles.title: La Torre Eiffel rusa sobrevivió a Stalin, a Hitler y a la caída de la URSS. Un siglo después, Moscú ha decidido que es más fácil copiarla que conservarla
articles.text:
Año 1922, la Unión Soviética levanta en Moscú una torre de acero que pretendía rivalizar con la Torre Eiffel de París. Aquella mole sobrevivió a Stalin, a la Segunda Guerra Mundial y a la desaparición del país que la había construido. Más de un siglo después, su futuro está en manos de las autoridades rusas, que consideran demasiado costoso restaurarla y plantean desmontarla para levantar una versión nueva. Sí, Rusia está dispuesta a conservar la idea de uno de sus mayores prodigios de ingeniería, incluso si para hacerlo tiene que destruirla.
La Torre Eiffel soviética. La Torre Shújov, situada al sur del centro de Moscú, fue encargada por Lenin y terminada en 1922. Diseñada por el ingeniero Vladímir Shújov, alcanza los 148 metros y está formada por una sucesión de estructuras hiperbólicas de acero entrelazado.
Su función era transmitir señales de radio por el territorio soviético y simbolizar las ambiciones tecnológicas del nuevo Estado comunista. La ligereza de su diseño la convirtió en una referencia de la arquitectura moderna y en una respuesta simbólica a la Torre Eiffel, inaugurada en París en 1889.
Un siglo resistiendo. La estructura atravesó las purgas estalinistas, la invasión alemana de la Unión Soviética y el colapso del régimen en 1991. Su deterioro llegó de una forma mucho menos espectacular, con décadas de mantenimiento insuficiente. La última vez que se pintó fue en 1964 y dejó de utilizarse en gran medida para las transmisiones a finales de 2001.
En 2014 ya existía un plan para derribarla, frenado por las protestas de especialistas rusos e internacionales. Tres años después se propuso desmontar las secciones superiores con un helicóptero para restaurarlas en un taller y reparar las inferiores sobre el terreno. Aquella intervención nunca se realizó.
Desmontar para reconstruir. Ahora, contaba el New York Times que el Ministerio de Cultura ruso ha modificado las condiciones de protección patrimonial del monumento, permitiendo su desmontaje completo sin exigir la conservación de todos sus elementos originales. La Red Rusa de Televisión y Radiodifusión, propietaria de la instalación, sostiene que el acero está demasiado deteriorado y que restaurarlo resultaría económicamente inviable.
Su propuesta consiste en recuperar las piezas que puedan aprovecharse y construir una nueva torre inspirada en el diseño de Shújov. Todavía no se han presentado públicamente planos detallados ni se ha explicado cuánto material histórico sobreviviría a la operación.
La factura de conservar la historia. La propietaria afirma que las alternativas de restauración estudiadas costarían miles de millones de rublos y que el presupuesto podría dispararse ante daños difíciles de evaluar. El historiador Airat Bagautdínov sostiene que esa incertidumbre ha pesado decisivamente en la elección del desmontaje.
Plus: la decisión llega en un contexto en el que Rusia prevé dedicar más de 200.000 millones de dólares a defensa el próximo año, mientras se reducen otras partidas. De hecho, el contraste ha alimentado las críticas sobre las prioridades presupuestarias del Kremlin.
La rebelión de los arquitectos. Explicaba el Times que especialistas rusos e internacionales han dirigido una carta abierta a Vladímir Putin para pedir que se paralice el proyecto y se revise el estado real de la estructura. Los firmantes argumentan que los estudios recientes indican que buena parte del acero original podría conservarse.
Entre quienes cuestionan la sustitución figura Barry Bergdoll, historiador de arquitectura de la Universidad de Columbia, que recuerda que la Torre Eiffel francesa ha sido restaurada repetidamente sin necesidad de reemplazarla por una copia. Para los defensores de Shújov, reproducir la silueta con acero moderno destruiría una parte esencial del valor histórico del monumento.
El futuro de una obra irrepetible. El calendario comunicado por las autoridades rusas el pasado 22 de octubre prevé preparar la obra este otoño, comenzar el desmontaje de la sección superior a principios de 2027 y retirar después las otras cinco secciones.
Los responsables del proyecto, por su parte, aseguran que intentarán conservar tantos elementos originales como sea posible, mientras los conservacionistas temen que la mayor parte termine sustituida. Así, tras sobrevivir a más de un siglo de convulsiones políticas y guerras, la Torre Shújov afronta una amenaza distinta e inesperada: que su silueta sobreviva mientras desaparece buena parte de la obra auténtica que la hizo célebre.

articles.title: New Android SMS of Death exploit can remotely crash unpatched phones
articles.text:
A security researcher has released a proof-of-concept exploit for a recently patched Android vulnerability, dubbed "SMS of Death" and tracked as CVE-2026-58882, that lets attackers remotely disrupt cellular service or crash phones by sending a specially crafted text message.
The zero-click denial-of-service flaw can interrupt ongoing calls, including emergency calls, without requiring any interaction from the target. What's worse, Android processes the message before it reaches the SMS inbox, leaving victims with no visible indication of what caused their phones to crash.
According to the vulnerability researcher, Mark Blah, Google reportedly patched the vulnerability in its October 2026 Android security updates for Android 14 through 17. However, the flaw is not listed in Google's October security bulletin, and older Android 12 and 13 devices remain vulnerable because they did not receive the fix.
Blah published a technical analysis of the flaw, caused by improper validation of a header-length value in Android's WapPushOverSms.decodeWapPdu function.
To exploit the flaw, an attacker can send the following malformed eight-byte WAP Push message to targeted phones:
01 06 88 80 80 80 00 BE   → sent as a data SMS to port 2948
When this value is translated into a signed 32-bit integer without a bounds check, it becomes -2147483648.
When Android attempts to allocate memory using this negative value, it triggers a NegativeArraySizeException that crashes the com.android.phone process.
As the com.android.phone process manages cellular functions, the crash disrupts mobile connectivity and disconnects ongoing phone calls, including calls to emergency services.
The researcher says the attack can also cause repeated crashes when carriers attempt to redeliver malicious messages or Android tries to process messages already stored on the phone.
When testing the flaw, the researcher found that sending 20 malicious messages could cause phones to get stuck in reboot loops. On one Android 12 device, the phone rebooted into recovery mode approximately every 90 seconds, requiring the user to perform a factory reset to recover.
A GitHub contributor named Sakis discovered a way to remove the malicious messages using Android Debug Bridge (ADB), but the process requires more advanced technical knowledge and access to a computer.
The researcher has published a proof-of-concept exploit that can send the malicious messages from another Android device.
Google's fix, titled "Fix remote DoS in decodeWapPdu," prevents the crashes by catching exceptions triggered when Android processes the malformed text messages.
The patch also deletes malicious messages from the SMS database to prevent them from triggering repeated crashes.
Android security updates are generally installed automatically on supported devices, but their availability depends on the device manufacturer and carrier, and a restart may be required to complete installation.
Now that a working proof-of-concept exploit has been released, Android users are strongly advised to install the latest security updates to protect their devices.

articles.title: This smart screwdriver uses a camera and AI to identify screws and set torque automatically
articles.text:
In brief: AI and machine learning are still largely associated with software, digital media, and PCs, but one company wants to show how the technology can improve power tools. Arrowmax's upcoming Arrowspace S1 electric screwdriver kit combines an HD camera, a smartphone app, toolcase LED lights, and an in-house AI model to take the guesswork out of identifying screws.
Hong Kong-based Arrowmax recently launched a Kickstarter campaign for what it calls the world's first AI-powered electric screwdriver, and funded it almost immediately. Starting at around $80, with shipments planned to begin in April 2027, the device aims to streamline the entire process of selecting a bit and driving a screw.
A rear-mounted contact probe rests on the screw head and holds the camera at a fixed distance while the S1's HD camera captures the screw. The probe helps ensure maximum accuracy when scanning tiny screws, like those on glasses.
The system identifies the screw's size and shape using an AI model that Arrowmax trained on tens of thousands of real-world photos. The company stresses that its in-house engineering team collected every sample without using external training data, addressing one of AI's main ethical concerns.
A companion smartphone app then displays the camera feed alongside controls for torque, gear mode, and other parameters. The S1 connects to the app over a local connection and doesn't require internet access.
Finally, LEDs in the connected smart case light up over the slot containing the recommended bit, and the screwdriver automatically adjusts its torque. The process is designed to make selecting the correct bit easier and to help prevent stripping, especially on the smallest screws.
An OLED display shows battery level, torque, and direction. A 600mAh LiPo battery ensures 90 minutes of runtime or about 900 screws, depending on torque settings. Torque ranges between 1 and 10 kgf/cm. Charging via the rear-mounted USB-C port takes around 70 minutes.
The standalone S1 screwdriver starts at $80, while a bundle that adds the smart case and 52 bits starts at $129 for early birds. The Kickstarter launched on October 20, met its goal within 24 hours, and has since surpassed it by more than an order of magnitude. Arrowmax has not provided a list of stretch goals. Add-ons include an $18 angle screw, two bit converter sets for $24 each, and a $40 mini bench vise.

articles.title: Elon Musk a un conseil pour votre argent. Surprise : il ne fait pas l'unanimité
articles.text:
Une nouvelle fois, Elon Musk a affirmé qu’il est dorénavant inutile d’épargner pour sa retraite. Selon le milliardaire sud-africain, nous pourrions tous (ou du moins les Américains) bénéficier d’un revenu universel, grâce aux bénéfices générés par l’IA. Une chose est sûre : cet avis ne fait pas l’unanimité.
Selon Elon Musk, il est devenu inutile d’épargner pour sa pension
Sur le réseau social X, une utilisatrice surnommée Viv a expliqué que « ses décisions financières douteuses […] n’auront plus d’importance dans quelques années », et ce en raison d’un « avenir d’abondance ». Elon Musk, qui passait par là, est venu confirmer cette hypothèse en affirmant qu’ « épargner de l’argent pour un avenir lointain est inutile avec l’avènement de l’abondance superintelligente ».
Selon Elon Musk, le développement de l’intelligence artificielle rendra l’épargne pour la retraite obsolète. Autant dire que cette déclaration n’est pas vraiment bien passée sur le réseau social dont il est le propriétaire. Certains pointent du doigt le fait qu’un milliardaire conseille de ne pas épargner, tandis que d’autres considèrent cette prémonition comme utopique, et donc dangereuse pour ceux qui seraient tentés de le croire sur parole.
En réalité, cela fait maintenant un moment qu’Elon Musk tient ce discours concernant l’épargne pour les pensions. En janvier dernier, lors du podcast Moonshots with Peter Diamandis, il avait déclaré : « Ne vous inquiétez pas trop à l’idée de mettre de l’argent de côté pour votre retraite. Dans dix ou vingt ans, cela n’aura plus d’importance. Vous n’aurez pas besoin d’épargner pour votre retraite si l’une des choses que nous avons évoquées se concrétise. Épargner pour la retraite deviendra alors tout simplement inutile ».
Le milliardaire sud-aficrain mise sur un revenu universel
Selon Elon Musk, les bénéfices engendrés par l’intelligence artificielle seront redistribués directement à la population. Une importante partie de la population n’effectuera plus un travail traditionnel, mais pourrait compter sur un revenu universel. Pour rappel, le milliardaire sud-africain a promis une action SpaceX « à chaque enfant en Amérique » en 2027.
De son côté, Anthropic, l’entreprise derrière l’IA Claude, a annoncé la création d’un fonds destiné à redistribuer une partie des bénéfices générés par l’IA à des ONG ou à « des populations spécifiques ». L’entreprise a d’ailleurs précisé que des personnes ayant perdu leur emploi à cause de l’IA pourraient bénéficier de ce fonds.
Alors, faut-il suivre l’avis d’Elon Musk et arrêter d’épargner pour sa retraite ? Pour sept experts en finances personnelles et en intelligence artificielle interrogés par Business Insider, la réponse est sans équivoque : non. En attendant, il est préférable de continuer à épargner pour sa retraite.

articles.title: Bill Gates (70 años), fundador de Microsoft, advierte sobre la IA: "Nunca ha existido un arma tan poderosa" y exige límites obligatorios por seguridad
articles.text:
La IA está avanzando a tal velocidad que plantea nuevas dificultades para controlar sus posibles usos maliciosos. Aunque las grandes compañías tecnológicas continúan desarrollando modelos cada vez más capaces, algunas de las figuras más importantes de la industria consideran que confiar exclusivamente en las empresas para garantizar su seguridad ya no es suficiente, y Bill Gates ha sido el último en sumarse a esta corriente.
El cofundador de Microsoft habló sobre esta cuestión en una entrevista concedida a NBC News en la que reclamó una mayor intervención de los gobiernos. Así, el empresario considera imprescindible establecer mecanismos de vigilancia y protección que las compañías estén obligadas a incorporar en sus sistemas.
Bill Gates cree que las empresas no pueden controlar la IA por sí solas
Durante la conversación, Gates aseguró que "nadie piensa que la autorregulación sea suficiente". Para el empresario, tanto los responsables políticos como las fuerzas de seguridad deben participar en la definición de las medidas de protección, sobre todo si existe la posibilidad de que estas herramientas se utilicen para cometer delitos o desarrollar ataques informáticos.
Cuando habla de las consecuencias que podría tener un uso malintencionado de la tecnología, su advertencia va un paso más lejos. Gates defiende que nunca ha existido un arma tan poderosa como la combinación de personas con malas intenciones y herramientas avanzadas de IA, así que menciona riesgos como los ciberataques contra infraestructuras como resultado de esto. Además, también habla de la posibilidad de que grupos pequeños adquieran capacidades que antes estaban reservadas a grandes Estados.
Pese a todo lo que compartió, Gates no propone paralizar el desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial. De hecho, su planteamiento consiste en incorporar sistemas de supervisión que permitan conocer qué están haciendo los modelos mientras se establecen medidas de seguridad obligatorias. Tal y como detalló, estas exigencias supondrían un coste adicional para las empresas sin frenar de forma considerable sus avances.
La dificultad estará en conseguir que gobiernos y compañías adopten criterios comunes, especialmente en un contexto de competencia tecnológica internacional. Gates considera que alcanzar acuerdos globales podría resultar incluso más complicado que las negociaciones sobre armamento nuclear durante la Guerra Fría. Su advertencia apunta a una cuestión fundamental para el futuro de la inteligencia artificial: quién debe supervisar sus capacidades y hasta dónde debería permitirse que actúe sin intervención humana.

articles.title: People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
articles.text:
People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
- Date:
- October 21, 2026
- Source:
- University of Pennsylvania School of Engineering and Applied Science
- Summary:
- Researchers analyzing nearly 150,000 Reddit posts uncovered unexpected symptom reports linked by users to unapproved versions of retatrutide, including increased appetite, sleep disturbances, and elevated heart rates. The findings differ from clinical trial results and highlight how AI could help identify potential drug safety signals that warrant further investigation.
- Share:
An experimental weight-loss drug that has not yet received regulatory approval is already attracting users willing to obtain unapproved versions online. Now, scientists are using artificial intelligence to investigate their experiences, uncovering unexpected symptom reports that differ from those documented in clinical trials.
The drug, retatrutide, belongs to a new generation of GLP-1 medications designed to help regulate appetite and body weight. Although it remains under investigation and is not approved for use, people are purchasing unapproved formulations that are not intended for human consumption and discussing their experiences on internet forums.
Researchers at the University of Pennsylvania analyzed nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments from approximately 40,000 users to investigate these accounts. Their study, published in JAMA Network Open, provides the first systematic examination of potential side effects reported by people claiming to use unapproved retatrutide.
One finding stood out. Among users whose reported symptoms could be classified, increased appetite was the most common complaint. That was particularly unexpected because retatrutide is designed to suppress hunger, and its Phase 2 clinical trials primarily identified digestive problems as the most frequent side effects.
AI Uncovers Unexpected Weight-Loss Drug Reports
"Our goal is to identify hypotheses in online conversations that we could test. AI helps us find recurring patterns in people's self-reports, including experiences that may be missed by conventional drug-safety monitoring," says Sharath Chandra Guntuku, Research Associate Professor in Computer and Information Science (CIS), Director of Penn's Computational Social Listening Lab and senior author of the study.
However, the researchers emphasize that the findings should not be interpreted as proof of previously unknown side effects. Reddit users represent a very different population from clinical trial participants, and their accounts cannot establish whether the drug caused the symptoms they described.
There is also considerable uncertainty about what these individuals are actually taking. Products sold outside regulated medical channels may differ from the genuine experimental medication in their ingredients, purity, and dosage.
"We can't say that retatrutide is causing these symptoms, or even that Reddit users are actually taking genuine retatrutide, since the drug is not legally available, and gray market formulations vary," says Lyle Ungar, Professor in CIS and a co-author of the study.
Rather than confirming new risks, the research offers scientists an opportunity to identify questions that warrant more rigorous investigation.
"This is the first glimpse into the experiences of a population that is otherwise outside conventional drug safety monitoring because they are taking unapproved versions of a drug that has yet to finish clinical trials," says Neil Sehgal, the study's first author and a doctoral student in CIS.
How Researchers Analyzed 150,000 Reddit Posts
The project builds on previous research by the University of Pennsylvania team. In that earlier investigation, scientists used large language models (LLMs), the type of artificial intelligence that powers many modern chatbots, to examine more than 400,000 Reddit posts discussing semaglutide and tirzepatide.
That analysis revealed reports of possible side effects, including menstrual irregularities, that may not have been fully documented in clinical trials or official drug safety records.
"We wanted to apply the same methodology to gray-market retatrutide," says Sehgal.
Retatrutide is particularly interesting because it works differently from existing GLP-1 medications. Semaglutide acts on one hormone receptor involved in blood sugar control and appetite regulation, while tirzepatide targets two. Retatrutide activates three receptors, potentially producing a different combination of effects throughout the body.
To investigate what people were experiencing, the researchers used AI to examine nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments. They identified approximately 14,000 users who claimed to have personally taken an unapproved version of retatrutide.
The AI systems then extracted descriptions of symptoms that users associated with the medication and translated those descriptions into standardized medical terminology. This allowed researchers to compare reports even when different people used different words to describe similar experiences.
After excluding expected effects such as weight loss and reduced appetite, the team identified 7,823 users who reported at least one symptom that could be medically classified.
"A researcher might be able to examine a few thousand Reddit posts by hand, but looking at nearly 150,000 would be an enormous undertaking," says Sehgal. "AI makes it possible to analyze these conversations at scale, identifying patterns in what people are sharing that would otherwise be difficult to recognize."
A Surprising Appetite Paradox Emerges
The most striking difference involved hunger.
In retatrutide's Phase 2 clinical trials (the drug is currently in Phase 3 trials, the final step before FDA approval), participants most commonly experienced gastrointestinal complaints, including nausea. These effects are familiar concerns with medications that influence appetite and digestion.
But among Reddit users who reported taking unapproved retatrutide, the pattern looked different. Increased appetite emerged as the most frequently described classifiable symptom, despite the substantial weight-loss effects demonstrated in clinical testing.
The researchers also compared the new findings with their earlier analysis of semaglutide and tirzepatide.
Compared with those earlier Reddit reports, discussions involving unapproved retatrutide contained proportionally more mentions of appetite-related changes, sleep disturbances, increased heart rate, and muscle-related symptoms. Reports of nausea and other digestive complaints were proportionally less common.
These differences could reflect how retatrutide interacts with the body. However, they could also result from differences between the groups of people discussing the medications, their other drug use, or the contents of the unapproved products.
"Retatrutide works differently from existing GLP-1 drugs, so it's possible that its effects on the body are different, too," says Jena Shaw Tronieri, Senior Research Investigator at Penn's Center for Weight and Eating Disorders and a co-author of the study.
"But the people discussing it on Reddit also may be different," she notes. "Users willing to obtain an unapproved medication on the gray market likely differ from other clinical populations. Some may be taking multiple experimental peptides, and we can't verify exactly what they're taking. We need more research to understand what, if anything, these differences in self-reported symptoms mean."
Can AI Detect Drug Safety Concerns Earlier?
Beyond the findings about retatrutide, the study demonstrates how AI could potentially improve the early detection of drug safety concerns.
Traditional monitoring systems depend heavily on clinical trials, reports submitted to regulators, and information collected by healthcare professionals. People obtaining experimental medications through unapproved channels may not be represented in those systems.
Social media offers another source of information, allowing researchers to identify recurring experiences that might otherwise escape attention. However, these reports must be independently investigated before they can be considered reliable evidence of a drug-related problem.
The Penn team has already seen an example of how this approach can help guide further research.
In their previous investigation of semaglutide and tirzepatide, researchers identified online reports of menstrual irregularities. Those findings subsequently encouraged another scientific team to examine similar symptoms using the FDA's database of reported adverse drug events.
The follow-up study, published in Obstetrics & Gynecology, also detected disproportionate reports of certain menstrual changes. Although those findings did not establish causation, they provided additional reasons to investigate the potential connection.
The researchers hope their retatrutide findings will lead to similar independent studies, particularly as the drug advances through clinical development.
"That's what we hope will happen with this study," says Sehgal. "Other researchers can take what we find on Reddit and look for the same patterns in other datasets, using entirely different methods. Whether those signals hold up or not, the goal is to build a better understanding of what people are actually experiencing."
The research was conducted through the University of Pennsylvania's School of Engineering and Applied Science and Perelman School of Medicine. Benjamin Rader of Boston Children's Hospital also contributed as a co-author. Funding was provided in part by the University of Pennsylvania's Penn Medical Communication Research Institute. Tronieri disclosed receiving an investigator-initiated grant from Novo Nordisk on behalf of the University of Pennsylvania, along with consulting fees from Currax Pharmaceuticals, LLC. No conflicts of interest were reported by the other authors.
